sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who uses the platform, what must it guarantee, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Names both users: agent builders who need tools fast and security who need attribution
Converts 2.4M calls a day into average and peak calls per second
Computes the monthly token cost of loading 60 tool definitions per turn
States a measurable target such as 100 percent of calls attributable to a user

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the layers from agent to downstream system and say what each hands over.
criteria: Puts a gateway on the path of every tool call rather than a client library
Separates identity (per-user downstream tokens) from policy (scope decisions)
Includes a durable workflow engine for approvals and onboarding
Includes an event log that feeds both audit and tool health

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What does the platform read, and how fresh must each source be?
criteria: Treats server manifests (tools/list output) as a source pulled on every release
Syncs identity groups and revokes tokens on offboarding
Leaves downstream ACLs in the downstream system instead of copying them

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How does a new server version get approved, and how is the call stream turned into live health?
criteria: Hashes a canonical form of the tool list so any description change is a new version
Runs a poisoning or prompt-injection test against new descriptions before approval
Rolls call events into per-tool error rate, latency and quota burn on a short interval

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: What model-driven pieces does the platform own, and how does it cut tool-definition tokens?
criteria: Proposes tool search or another way to send fewer tool definitions per turn, with a token or dollar estimate
Searches only within the tools the agent is granted
Keeps the chosen tool set stable within a session so prompt caching still works
Requires human approval on write tools rather than trusting a review model alone

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What state does the platform keep, where, and for how long?
criteria: Keys downstream tokens by user and provider, never by agent
Stores refresh tokens encrypted in a secrets store such as Vault
Stores idempotency keys for write tools
Avoids keeping tool results beyond a short cache

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: How are servers of different provenance hosted, isolated and versioned?
criteria: Sandboxes third-party and code-execution servers with a named technology and an egress allowlist
Never forwards the agent's platform token to a server (no token passthrough)
Describes a staged rollout for a new server version with a rollback condition
Handles legacy services that cannot do OAuth

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What endpoints exist, and where do the 40 ms of overhead go?
criteria: Exposes MCP over Streamable HTTP with one endpoint per agent or an equivalent aggregation
Includes a kill switch endpoint with a stated propagation time
Gives a latency budget split by stage that sums to the 40 ms p95
Sizes the gateway fleet and says whether load or availability drives it

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached, with what key and TTL, and what must never be cached?
criteria: Caches downstream access tokens with refresh before expiry and single-flight on 401
Includes the user in any tool-result cache key
Caches only read-only, idempotent results, with a TTL in seconds

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Which stores hold what, how big are they, and what does the platform cost per month?
criteria: Sizes the audit store from events per day, bytes per event and 400 days
Uses immutable storage (such as S3 Object Lock or a hash chain) for the audit trail
Records tool version, schema hash and policy version on each audit event
Gives a monthly infra cost and compares it with the $45k budget

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does a tool call return to the agent, including when it is denied?
criteria: Caps result size and paginates large results
Returns denials and rate limits as typed, machine-readable results with a retry hint
Marks content from external systems as untrusted data

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: Which controls stop a misbehaving agent, and where do they live?
criteria: Computes effective permission as the intersection of user and agent scopes, default deny, in code
Gates named high-risk write tools behind human approval with a timeout
Splits shared downstream quotas per team with priority for interactive traffic
States that no permission or limit lives in a prompt or tool description

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: Which numbers prove the platform worked, and how are they measured?
criteria: Gives baselines and targets for at least three metrics
Measures shadow paths by reconciling downstream audit logs with gateway events
Includes onboarding time or another adoption metric, not only security metrics

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, what catches it, and what fails open or closed?
criteria: Covers identity provider outage and audit pipeline outage
States explicitly which calls fail closed and which degrade
Covers a server whose description changes after approval

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it in six months, and what number ends each phase?
criteria: Puts traffic through the gateway before adding restrictions
Ends every phase with a measurable number
Fits the plan into 26 weeks for 8 engineers
